chapter: Glen Gray band: Red Nichols and Bobby Hackett
title: Nichols's solo on Don't Take Your Love from Me and his departure
summary: Challis wrote Nichols a chorus, which was one of his best, then Nichols fronted the band when Gray was ill and left claiming he was held down.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Where does Hackett come into this?

Oh, I'm getting to it. Well, anyway, I guess I'm a little too detailed, but I want to lay that thing for -- anyway, it got to the point where he -- he wanted some solos to do. He was in the band about six months, and by the time we got around to it, I had made him a chorus, and put a nice background in for him on a record. I don't think you'd be familiar with it. I don't know what the name -- da-da-dee-dee-

"Don't Take Your Love from Me." I think that's one of the best solos he ever played. Now, he came into the studio, and he played it over, and we had the arrangement about two weeks before, and by the time he finished it, polished it off to play, it was -- he was the old Red Nichols.

He had made a nice chorus, and I was never a great admirer of what he played, but he did an awfully nice job. And he wanted more. Finally he quit, you know. Then he wanted to front the band, and he did. Glen Gray took sick, and I think he later died from the -- got cancer. He went to the clinic up in Boston. And Red took over. This was the, over at the old Pennsylvania Hotel.

Well, after that, I guess, the way things turned out, he figured he's well enough and good enough to go on his own. So he leaves the band and he tells your old magazine, I think -- Down Beat -- I don't think he could remember -- that he didn't get any kind of good treatment there in the Glen Gray band, that they were trying to stifle him, hold him down, something like that. I don't know who would have written that article.

Yes, that's right. Well, anyway, it came out. So we didn't pay too much attention to it. But he went out, and he got a band, and he started his second time around, and he got a fine band. I heard him out in Los Angeles.
